lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.criterion: Human connection, communication quality, and dignified closure
findings.observation: The frozen artifact demonstrates a recruiter-only evidence and state-review loop, not a candidate experience. It explicitly stops before sending a message or changing an external system, and the bundle contains no candidate-facing preview, receipt, correction path, delay update, rejection, withdrawal, or closure state.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; artifact.json scenario.task and intentionally_unavailable; ios-today-light.png (sha256 4f4df9f8b9d5e1ce131c60b2881b6b400987ed3e960ad5ec341ae579a1984517) shows only the recruiter Today surface; RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:55-59 and 270-274 state that the change is internal and external action requires separate approval; CandidateSignalUITests.swift:90-107 verifies only a local handoff with no external changes.
findings.user_impact: The product may protect a candidate from an accidental send, but this evidence cannot show that the candidate is kept informed, can correct a misunderstanding, can reply on reasonable terms, or receives humane closure. A polished recruiter draft is not proof of candidate trust, and a 99-point candidate experience claim would be unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Add the smallest synthetic recipient-facing proof without sending anything: a recruiter-reviewed message preview that names the specific unresolved point, acknowledges uncertainty, identifies the human owner and response commitment, and gives the candidate an easy correction, channel-preference, or no-further-contact path. Include delayed-client and respectful-closure variants rather than a generic upbeat template.
findings.verification: Run synthetic end-to-end scenarios for clarification, hiring-manager delay, withdrawal, and rejection; inspect the exact candidate-visible content and recruiter handoff receipt; verify no send occurs without separate approval, the recipient has an easy response/correction path, and every waiting or closure state has a named human owner and promised time. Then obtain authorized candidate feedback before claiming candidate-experience quality.

findings.observation: The default surface calls itself Today but hard-codes Friday, August 7 and relative statuses such as 5h and Answer due Friday. The artifact is dated August 24, and the main screenshot does not visibly mark these timestamps as fixture-only or stale.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 dated 2026-08-24; ios-today-light.png shows FRIDAY, AUGUST 7, Needs review / 5h, and Answer due Friday; RelationshipArchiveView.swift:178-181 and 241-253 hard-code those values; the screenshot hash matches artifact.json.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can treat stale timing as current and interrupt a candidate or client at the wrong moment. Even though this build has no external effect, the default attention signal is not yet trustworthy enough to guide humane follow-through.
findings.recommendation: Derive dates and elapsed time from canonical timestamps and timezone, show evidence freshness beside the reason for attention, and visibly label synthetic fixture time on the main surface. When recency is unknown or expired, ask the recruiter to revalidate context before proposing contact.
findings.verification: Launch on a date different from the fixture date and verify that Today shows the actual local date or an unmistakable synthetic-fixture label; inject expired evidence and verify the UI marks it stale and does not present a current-contact recommendation until revalidated.

findings.observation: The UI usefully says that one client answer is holding the candidate's decision, but it does not show who owns that answer, when they committed to respond, what has already been tried, or how the recruiter should recover after a missed commitment. Answer due Friday is a date, not accountable collaboration.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; ios-today-light.png shows One client answer is holding her decision and Remote work from Singapore remains unresolved; RelationshipArchiveView.swift:197-213 names the dependency, while lines 249-253 provide only Answer due Friday; no frozen screenshot, source path, or test demonstrates a named client or hiring-manager owner, escalation, or missed-deadline recovery.
findings.user_impact: Without visible internal ownership, the candidate can still bear the cost of client delay through silence or another unnecessary chase. That is an internal collaboration failure leaking into the candidate relationship.
findings.recommendation: Attach a named client or hiring-manager owner, promised response time, last follow-up, and a humane missed-deadline path to the dependency. The smallest safe next step should route attention to that internal owner and prepare a candid candidate update only when there is something material to say.
findings.verification: Simulate a missed client commitment and verify that Today prompts the named internal owner or escalation path, does not generate a repeated candidate nudge, and keeps ownership of any candidate update or closure visible until a human completes it.

strengths: The review puts exact quoted evidence and provenance before the proposed state, then explains that confirming the relationship state does not send a message or write externally (RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:17-59).

Keep unresolved, Confirm change, and Undo decision are explicit recruiter controls, and the receipt truthfully repeats that no message or external system changed (RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:61-93 and 461-495).

The Today surface names the client-side dependency and reports 14 relationships needing no action, which is a healthier attention model than nudging every candidate because automation is available (RelationshipArchiveView.swift:187-263).

The Guide is constrained to supported evidence and draft authority, and the UI tests explicitly refuse response-speed, tone, interests, fit, quality, personality, and acceptance scoring (RelationshipArchiveView.swift:473-494; RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:303-376; CandidateSignalUITests.swift:118-131).
missing_evidence: No candidate-facing screenshot, message preview, notification, delivery receipt, correction interaction, or candidate-authored feedback is in the frozen bundle.
No waiting-state journey shows how a candidate is updated when a recruiter, client, or hiring manager misses a commitment.
No rejection, withdrawal, opt-out, no-further-contact, or respectful closure journey is implemented or tested in the frozen evidence.
No evidence shows recipient channel preference, timing preference, informed consent scope, or a human support/escalation path.

The recorded pnpm ios:check result is failed because testRelationshipCaptureRequiresCurrentOwnerAndCompilesGoldWiki did not complete after the authorized localhost relationship fixture was unavailable; the separate localhost sync test was skipped, so the full tested journey is not green.

Real candidate data, production authentication, external writes, recruiter field evidence, real-device evidence, VoiceOver-user evidence, and field outcome evidence are intentionally unavailable and must not be treated as passed.
open_questions: When the remote-policy answer is late, which human owns the update to Leila and what response commitment will she be given?
At the first candidate-facing step, how can Leila correct the remote-versus-relocation interpretation or state a preferred channel and timing without pressure?
How will the product distinguish a synthetic fixture date from current relationship truth on the default Today surface?
